newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - BME/Reuters German April PMI index.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - BME/Reuters German April PMI index.

text.p: Following are reactions of economists to publication of the BME/Reuters German Purchasing Managers' Index for April, which rose to a seasonally-adjusted 56.58 from 54.58 in March, reaching its highest level yet since calculations began 12 months ago.
On an unadjusted basis, the index also hit a record of 57.93, up from 56.43 in March. A reading of the PMI above 50 indicates the manufacturing economy is expanding.

LARRY ANDERSON, HEAD OF RESEARCH, BAYERISCHE VEREINSBANK: "These figures confirm the anecdotal evidence that we are getting from the companies that we cover and makes us more confident in our forecast that the German economy is set for quite a sharp jump in the second quarter.

However, we would be sceptical of saying that things are booming in the German economy. Exports -- BMWs, Volkswagens and so on -- are doing okay but this probably overstates the growth in the economy as a whole.

(On unemployment), the new index only shows the industrial side of the economy -- and there won't be any new jobs there, rather the trend is to reduce jobs. Employment needs to be created in the service sector, which is fairly weak at the moment.

HANS-JUERGEN MELTZER, DB RESEARCH: My impression is that the index has an optimistic bias as it is in contrast to the output figures given in yesterday's (government) production numbers. My assumption is that the index overstates development because of the short history of seasonally-adjusted data (which could lead to variations) in incoming orders and other variables.

(On linkage to jobs data due later), even if we are expecting a decline in the seasonally-adjusted figures...this is only a reflection of the improvement in the construction sector, which is weather-related."
